record.paper_title: Open Problems in Efficient Semi-Supervised PAC Learning
record.original_question: Suppose every variable is either a positive indicator or a negative indicator, and replace the strict compatibility condition from the monotone-disjunction example with a margin-style requirement: a positive example must contain at least 60% of the positive indicators and at most 40% of the negative indicators, while a negative example must satisfy the analogous reversed condition. The open question is whether this two-sided-majority-with-margins setting admits a computationally efficient semi-supervised PAC learning algorithm with labeled-sample complexity matching the small compatible-search-space intuition up to polynomial factors.

evidence.quote: Two-sided majority with margins: As a different generalization of the problem from Section 3.1, suppose that again every variable is either a positive or negative indicator, but we relax the margin condition a bit. In particular, say we require that x either contain at least 60% of the positive indicators and at most 40% of the negative indicators (for positive examples) or vice versa (for negative examples).
The high-level question is whether for interesting classes C and notions of compatibility χ, one can learn with this many (or polynomial in this many) labeled examples by efficient algorithms.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Setting. Fix a Boolean domain {0,1}^n whose coordinates are partitioned into two unknown disjoint sets: a set P of "positive indicator" variables and a set N of "negative indicator" variables, with P ∪ N = {1,…,n}. For an example x ∈ {0,1}^n, write p(x) = (number of indices i ∈ P with x_i = 1)/|P| and q(x) = (number of indices i ∈ N with x_i = 1)/|N| (fractions of positive and negative indicators that are "on" in x).

Target concepts. A target concept is specified by a partition (P,N) as above. Given a distribution D over {0,1}^n, the target labels examples as follows:
 • x is labeled +1 if p(x) ≥ 0.6 and q(x) ≤ 0.4;
 • x is labeled −1 if p(x) ≤ 0.4 and q(x) ≥ 0.6.
We assume D is supported on examples satisfying one of these two conditions (i.e., the target is consistent on the support of D).

Semi-supervised PAC framework. The learner receives (i) an arbitrarily large pool of unlabeled examples drawn i.i.d. from D and (ii) m labeled examples drawn i.i.d. from D and labeled by the target. For inputs ε, δ ∈ (0,1), the learner must output, with probability at least 1−δ, a hypothesis h whose error under D is at most ε.

Notion of compatibility. A partition (P,N) is called compatible with D if D is concentrated on the union of the two margin sets above (every example in the support satisfies one of the two inequalities). Let χ(D) denote the set of partitions compatible with D; intuitively, when this set is small, few labeled examples should be required to identify the target among compatible hypotheses.

Question. Does there exist an algorithm that, given polynomially many unlabeled examples, runs in time polynomial in n, 1/ε, 1/δ, and uses a number of labeled examples polynomial in log|χ(D)|, 1/ε, 1/δ (matching, up to polynomial factors, the labeled sample complexity suggested by the size of the compatible search space), to PAC-learn the class of two-sided-majority-with-margins concepts described above?
artifact.status_search_result: A web search surfaces the original open-problems write-up and Balcan–Blum's augmented PAC model papers, but no follow-up work that explicitly resolves the "two-sided majority with margins" variant. No source confirming a solution (positive or negative) was located, so the status is recorded as unknown.
